challenges.challenge_text: The Ravik headline of no net shortfall (-46.5%) rests on a direct rail gain that Loki's own claim-loki-105 says cannot be quantified. The Tier 1 Ravik notice states it gives no volume moved, no share of lost trade carried and no tariff, and the minister's 'covers all of the exports Orvan has lost' line is an interested-party assertion from the body promoting the route. Crediting an unquantified rail gain as a negative shortfall, while also saying rail growth cannot be measured, is internally inconsistent. The -46.5% figure is also a direct-row change, not a net Ravik cell result. The defensible Ravik estimate should carry the rail offset as unknown, not as a documented gain.

The Tolan low end (50.8%) credits Vanir substitute growth in full, but Loki's own mechanism treats the Vanir wheat as the documented substitute. The Tier 2 Anchor Marine report says the Vanir volumes are smaller than the Orvan trade lost, and that the parcels are smaller than the Orvan cargoes they replace. A full-credit low end overstates the offset that the source supports. Anchor Marine is a port operator that does not trade grain, so its statement is usable for the scale of substitution but not for the price or volume offset itself. The cell should not take full credit at the low end.

challenges.challenge_text: The high bound of 60.3% comes from calc-r1-thor-02's no_credit scenario, which gives zero credit to the Vanir substitute. The Tolan substitute route is documented in ORV-0044 P6 and P7: Vanir wheat to Tolan reached USD 26.5M and 67,000 t in November 2026, and USD 25.7M and 65,000 t in December 2026. Those figures are above the November and December 2025 values of USD 19.6M / 53,000 t and USD 18.9M / 51,000 t (ORV-0044 P12, P13). The calc's own substitute pass shows a substitute value change of +18.1% to +26.2%, yet the envelope never credits it in the high bound. The claim's 'net_value_shortfall_pct' label also does not match the calc's gross figure, so the net figure after substitute credit is not shown. ORV-0044 P14 adds that the gain 'does not replace the Orvan sea volume', which is a reason to qualify the range, not to ignore the credit.

The claim treats the full Midgard maize drop (38.5%) as lost exposure. The only source for the mechanism says part of the maize trade ran on delayed delivery terms, and it attributes the October volume holding up to that. Delayed-delivery terms defer cargoes rather than remove them, so the October-to-December drop (146,000 t to 75,000 t and 74,000 t) is not a clean measure of lost supply. The claim does not net out any deferred cargo or the terms that the same source describes. The point estimate is also a single value (low = high = 38.5), so it carries no uncertainty for timing. The source is Tier 1, so the deferral mechanism should be stated and the range widened, not dropped.

The claim says the four TRADE_ROW_REPEATED_VALUES rows barely move the figure, so the 56.3%–56.7% range is robust. The calc's without_flagged pass rests on only two paired months (2026-09 and 2026-10, per calc-r1-thor-05), against four months in the with_flagged pass. The two passes are not comparable, so the 'nearly unchanged' reading is not supported. The flagged rows are the July 2026, August 2026, November 2026 and December 2026 entries. They are the very rows that set the range, and the claim does not say whether repeated values reflect a data error or a true flat month. The range should be shown as sensitive to these four rows until they are checked against a later source.
